rebuttal_response: The claim that manifest ownership overrides the implementation pattern does not survive scrutiny. P02S remains unauthorized to edit live structured files, while P09 explicitly applies the P02S YAML codemod and owns `ci_workflow_updates`. Adding a broad ownership label does not transfer the actual mutation responsibility; it instead creates overlapping ownership.

findings.title: Structured-file edits remain owned and executed outside P02S
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 4: “P02S owns all structured file edits” and “no other prompt owns structured-file transformation units.”
findings.trigger: P09 updates a structured CI workflow YAML file, or any downstream prompt applies another live TOML/JSON/YAML transformation.
findings.consequence: A prompt other than P02S owns and performs a structured-file edit, defeating the required exclusive ownership and codemod gate.
findings.evidence: The manifest gives P02S the broad label `structured_file_transformations_all_formats`, but P02S still says, “Do not edit live TOML/JSON/YAML files; downstream owners apply the proven codemod.” P09 explicitly says it will use the P02S YAML codemod and owns `ci_workflow_updates`; P02S authorized paths contain no live structured-file targets.

findings.title: The existing v1 manifest was replaced instead of preserving a new version
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 7: “Confirm no existing artifacts overwritten with new versions” and pass condition requiring “prior artifacts unchanged.”
findings.trigger: A reviewer or operator attempts to verify the manifest used in rounds 1 and 2 against the active v1 artifact.
findings.consequence: The original v1 evidence is no longer available at its prior version identity, breaking immutable artifact lineage and preventing byte-for-byte verification of the earlier checkpoint state.
findings.evidence: Round 1 used `prompt_manifest.resolved.v1.yaml` with different paths and statuses. Checkpoint v3 says the manifest “stays v1.yaml,” records corrections within it, and states that the v2 manifest was removed. The active v1 now contains altered paths, statuses, timestamp, and ownership rather than preserving those changes under a new version.

observations: P00A-B01 is resolved: the required v1 path exists, contains 13 entries, uses existing prompt paths, and all downstream entries are now marked active.
The active manifest has 25 listed ownership labels, all textually unique and non-empty; the semantic structured-file overlap is captured under P00A-B02.
The P00A schema validator still succeeds, and current working-tree changes remain within authorized planning paths.
The broad rollback commands remain a non-blocking concern.
reasoning: The history accurately records both verdicts I personally issued. I verified checkpoint v3, the active manifest, its prompt paths and statuses, current repository status, and the supplied artifact digest. B01 is repaired. B02 survives because actual live structured mutations remain assigned outside P02S. The reuse and alteration of the prior v1 manifest independently defeats Criterion 7, so PASS is not available.
